#5118. The 7 Best Pubic Hair Trimmers in 2026, Tested by Grooming Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

These are the only tools I trust near my, er, tool.

LISTEN, NO ONE is going to say you must trim your pubic hair, but a little over half of all men do. Shaving, trimming, or hell, even getting a manzillian, comes down to a personal decision in both the how and why. Some guys like the way it feels, some like the way it looks, and some get a confidence boost knowing that they’re well-groomed down there. Whatever your reasons for below-the-belt manscaping, the most important thing to consider before you start is what tools you’re going to use to do it.

Trimmers are a great option for body grooming because they offer a variety of options. Most of them, at least the ones designed for the delicate groin area, have features to help protect the skin on your penis, scrotum, and surrounding areas from nicks and cuts.

They also usually have length attachments so you can choose exactly how long you want your hair (and even change it up as desired). Still, if you favor a close, hairless shave, you may want to turn to your old standbys: a razor and shaving cream. Whichever tool you ultimately choose will come down to a few factors based on your unique preferences. These are the seven best options across the board.

When it comes to pubic hair trimming, it’s all about balancing risk versus results. When you’re trimming or shaving delicate skin below the belt, you need to be careful, and this trimmer helps minimize risk. Specifically designed for your groin area, the blades are more closely spaced to help prevent snags, and the attachments help protect your skin from direct contact with the razor.

Testing Notes: This trimmer makes the case for using tools specifically designed for the area you’re grooming. I found in my testing that its blades are more closely placed than your traditional trimmer to help prevent skin from being caught between them. They actually make a difference when trimming your delicate nether regions.

All the features packed into this trimmer make the experience of trimming your groin as easy as possible and minimize cut risk, while the skin-protecting attachment does a great job of providing further distance between your skin and the blade. The one thing to note about this trimmer, however, is that if you prefer a clean shave, this will not deliver it by itself.

While it will trim very close, even with the attachment, it’s not going to give you a smooth, clean finish. You may want to use this trimmer to trim down the carpet first before moving in with a traditional razor. Also, if you’re hoping to trim other parts of your body, like your head or face (which I wouldn’t recommend for sanitary reasons), you may not find this trimmer powerful enough for the thicker hair that’s found in those locations.

Honestly, is there something the Philips OneBlade can’t do? Since its launch, this trimmer and shaver has become an iconic grooming essential, and for good reason. It’s incredibly easy to use, hardly ever nicks or cuts skin, and can shave and trim with equally good results. This version even comes with more length attachments that allow you to get your ideal manscaping results with ease.

Testing Notes: In all of my trimmer and shaver testing, no matter what kind, the Philips OneBlade stands out among the pack because it’s just so darn easy to use. Unlike your typical trimmers, the innovative head is shaped like a razor and can cut hair in both directions, making it foolproof.

There is also something about the razor, even when used without any attachments, that hardly ever cuts skin, even when you’re using it on your delicate areas below the belt. Since it’s designed for body grooming, the OneBlade features more attachments than the original, but you still won’t be able to leave hair super long.

The plus side of getting quite as close as other trimming options means it’s nearly impossible to cut yourself—even if you’re using it without a guard. Whenever someone is nervous about nicking their nuts, this is my top recommendation.

It’s best for people who like a close trim or a shave. The small size and light weight make it easy to take with you wherever you go, and I had no issue with the battery life, even though it’s not quite as long as some others on this list.

I also appreciate that it comes with a second blade, so you can easily switch them when you use this on your face (you don’t want to use the same blade on your face and body because of the possibility of cross-contamination).

Read more: Philips Norelco OneBlade Review

This trimmer is chock-full of cool features that are the sort of thing you didn’t know you needed until you have them, like a built-in LED light for seamless groinal navigation, a travel lock to avoid slicing through clothes or other products in your Dopp kit, and a nifty low-battery light to let you know it’s time to recharge before diving into a trim.

This trimmer is built for below-the-belt grooming but works great on other body parts too. It trims quickly and efficiently, no matter where you use it. The 5.0 is also fully waterproof and armed with a protective outer guard above the blades to minimize the risk of nicks or cuts.

Testing Notes: In my testing, I found a lot to love about the newest version of the Lawn Mower. Compared to previous models, it seems to cut a little bit easier and more efficiently, and with less snagging. The blade guard really does help in this department, though I did experience a few nicks when trying to trim too quickly (never a good idea when dealing with the groin, to be honest).

I don’t recommend using it without the guard, as the blades can be a little harsh on bare skin. However, a natural side effect of this is that you won’t ever get a completely bald shave with this device. Still, it’s surprisingly lightweight, and the added features like the built-in light make the experience of groin trimming as pleasant as it can be. It also corrected one of the more annoying issues with previous models by adding a travel lock on its power button that requires more effort to activate.

Unlike previous models, the 5.0 does not include a charging dock; however, it is fully equipped with USB-C charging capabilities, which I much prefer to the dock. I’d argue that every electric device should be required to use this much more universal charger. It saves on space by limiting the amount of wires you need laying around, and is far more convenient to replace if you ever lose the included cord.

Read More: Manscaped Chairman Plus Review

Meridian’s body trimmer helps prevent irritation, tugging, and nicks with its high-precision ceramic blades. Slicing your skin when manscaping, especially if you’re new to it, can produce serious panic, which is why Meridian went with ceramic blades. In comparison to steel or plastic, ceramic blades stay sharper longer, generate less heat, and glide smoothly across sensitive skin.

This makes Meridian’s trimmer ideal for beginners or anyone nervous about trimming sensitive areas. Plus, it’s waterproof and easy to use. There aren’t any complicated settings or tech involved, and just two guards to choose from. For beginners, this is perfect. It limits any learning curve beyond getting over the initial hump of anxiety for where you’re taking a blade.

Testing Notes: Meridian highlights two key benefits of its pubic trimmer: safety and speed—even claiming you can finish a full job in under 60 seconds. While I can confirm it’s powerful enough to mow through hair fast, no one should approach grooming with that expectation. Rushing, especially on sensitive areas, is a quick way to end up with nicks and cuts.

In terms of safety, I found this trimmer rarely—if ever—caused cuts or irritation. However, that safety seems to come at the cost of precision. I often had to go over the same spot multiple times to get a close shave. While the ceramic blades boost protection, they just don’t shave as closely as stainless steel.

Braun built this trimmer to power through all kinds of hair, no matter the length or location. With adjustable settings offering up to 40 lengths, it trims nose hairs just as easily as it delivers a crew cut. Its powerful motor and precision make it a top choice for anyone with thick body hair or an untamed look down below, where other trimmers often fall short.

Testing Notes: I love the wide-ranging length options the Braun All-In-One Series 9 offers that allow for true head-to-toe grooming. The adjustable length dial particularly makes transitioning from one part of your body to another seamless and quick for those in a hurry. Now, I wouldn’t recommend using the same trimmer for your face and body, but this device certainly has the agility and horsepower to handle all areas smoothly.

I also dig how sleek the charging dock is and, crucially, how little space it takes up on the bathroom counter. That being said, while Braun boasts about the Series 9’s 180-minute charging runtime, my testing found it’s in the 120-minute range. Still an impressive burst from one charge, but not quite 180 minutes.

Read More: Braun Series 9 Style Kit Review

Using a disposable razor for pubic shaving is great because it minimizes the risk of cross-contamination, and you ensure that your blades are always sharp and ready to cut. This disposable razor has five gentle blades that, while not specifically designed for the groin, are designed for the most sensitive skin, making it perfect for the area.

Testing Notes: Conventional wisdom says that using fewer blades is ideal for shaving the pubic area, as razors with multiple blades often increase the risk of irritation, razor bumps, and ingrown hairs. These issues tend to arise when the blades cut hair beneath the skin’s surface, creating friction and complicating regrowth.

In contrast, a single- or double-blade razor trims hair cleanly at the surface, reducing skin damage and delivering a smoother, gentler shave. But I found the BIC Flex 5 Sensitive razor to be the best of both worlds. Covering the ground of a five-blade razor with the softness of a one-blade razor.

Not only did it speed up the admittedly long process of pubic shaving, but it did so without destroying my most delicate skin. The only trade-off here is that this razor doesn’t get quite as close as other, less-gentle blades. Still, it gets much closer than the trimmers on this list, and nearly as close as the Gillette Intimate Razor. Besides, going entirely bald down here is rarely a goal of mine, so I saw this as a positive.

If you’re looking to go as close to bald as possible, this is your best option. Designed specifically for body grooming, this razor features a compact, ultra-grippy handle that minimizes the risk of dropping and helps you maintain control while in the shower (or contorting yourself to reach every part of your groin). The blades are about as spaced out from each other as I’ve seen on any razor, which helps prevent clogging—something that is even more common when dealing with thick body hair.

Surrounding the two blades are a lubricating strip, an anti-ingrown bar, and an anti-irritation bar that work to reduce friction and help prevent trapped hairs. Plus, the blade head sits on a flexible pivoting disc, which helps the razor follow the contours of your body for smoother, more consistent contact with the skin.

Testing Notes: I’m not usually one to go completely bald below the waist, but this razor makes a strong case for it. It left my skin smooth and irritation-free without any lingering bumps in the days following, which is something I’ve found to be common when dealing with body razors. The grip is incredible and the pivoting head makes getting into the nooks and crannies of your body easy.

Before diving into the most intimate of manscaping, it’s important to consider a few key components of the device you’ll be using, given the sensitivity of the region. Not only to avoid any dreaded nicks or cuts, but also to ensure that the process is completed as seamlessly as possible.

Whenever you’re dealing with a trimmer of any kind, the battery life is one of the most prominent considerations. No one wants their device to sputter out and die when they’ve only managed to trim half their beard, and the same is true for the nether regions. Sure, it may be less noticeable than having half a beard, but it can still be uncomfortable. Look for devices that can hold a charge for at least an hour; this should guarantee you two to three sessions per charge.

Any less and you’re going to have to really be diligent with charging after every use or run the risk of it dying out before the next job’s done. The easiest way to avoid this scenario is to look for a rechargeable device, but more on that in a sec.

If you’re a committed pubic trimmer and never travel without one, look for the lighter options to ensure you can comfortably keep them in a carry-on or bag without weighing yourself down. While the TSA and airlines do not generally have a weight limit specifically for grooming devices, they do limit the weight of your bags, so we recommend sticking to trimmers that are under 10 oz to avoid too much bulk. Plus, if you’re new to this type of thing, steering away from tools that are heavier than this until you get a better idea of the process will help you avoid any painful slip-ups.

Similarly, how often do you change up your overall manscaping look? If you find yourself often changing up lengths and styles, you’re going to want to grab a device with multiple attachments and length options. The Braun Series 9 is the best-case scenario here, as it comes packed with nine attachments that create a total of 40 (!) length options. On the other hand, if you typically go full bald or keep it one consistent length, focus on the device’s head shape and blade material or close shaving ability rather than the number of attachments.

For the closest shave (outside of a cartridge razor), look to stainless steel or metal blades, as these can handle the most motor power and are more adept at plowing through thicker hair. While most of the trimmers on this list (and pubic trimmers in general) do not list their official motor power, having stainless steel blades is often the best indicator of a powerful tool, as it shows the brand looks towards the highest quality materials and performance available.

Not to mention, stainless steel blades are typically easier to clean. That being said, the risk of nicks and cuts is higher, so if you’re new to pubic trimming, opt for ceramic or plastic blades. These are gentler on skin, though they won’t get you as close to bare skin.

Use a rechargeable pubic trimmer to avoid mid-trim shutdowns and eliminate the need for spare batteries. Keep it charged between 30 percent and 80 percent to maintain performance and prevent it from dying when you need it most.

Do you prefer to do your manscaping in or outside of the shower? There is no wrong answer, but whichever you prefer is worth keeping in mind when choosing a trimmer. Some are made to be used wet, like the Philips Norelco OneBlade, while others not so much. If you’re a dedicated shower groomer, focus on the fully waterproof options.

As Men’s Health’s grooming editor, I test electric razors and similar devices for a living. When it comes to pubic trimmers, we’ve been testing these devices for nearly three years since this story was first published in 2023. For this update, I tested or retested over 15 pubic trimmers and razors, while consulting with skin and haircare experts on which tools they recommend in 2026.

I also considered top-reviewed trimmers that had high customer ratings on trusted e-commerce websites. After putting each device to the test, I evaluated its effectiveness, safety, and value. Following 12 months of testing, these seven tools proved to be the best for the job.

1. First and foremost, make sure you have ample time and are not rushed. This is not something you want to speed through.

2. Position yourself in front of a mirror with good lighting to make sure you have good visibility for all the crevices.

3. Grab your trimmer and pick your desired length. If you plan to fully shave your pubic hair, set the length long enough to shave easily but not too long—about a couple of days’ worth of stubble. If you’re trimming, start with a longer setting than you want at first; you can always trim it shorter later.

4. Apply baby powder on your pubic area while it’s dry to help soak up extra moisture and plump up the hair.

5. With short, gentle strokes, use the trimmer to cut the hair. Pubic hair grows in a variety of directions, so you’ll want to go slow and possibly go over the same areas a few times. For your scrotum and shaft, go extra slow and stretch the skin to flatten it and make it easier to trim. If you’re trimming your buttcheeks, crack, or perineum, you may want to place a hand mirror on the floor to help see where you’re trimming. You can also place one leg on a tub or toilet to make the area easier to see.

6. If you’re happy with the trim job, then you’re done! Hop in the shower to wash off.

7. If you’re going to shave completely, once you’re out of the shower, apply a pre-shave oil and shaving cream to the areas you’re going to shave. The key here is not to be stingy with the cream.

8. When you’re taking a razor to your nether regions, you’ll want to be extra careful. Shave with the grain of the hair in short, slow strokes. Do not—I repeat—do not rush. You’ll want to use the same stretching technique on your scrotum and shaft as you did while trimming, and the mirror is ideal if you’re taking the razor around back.

9. Make sure to rinse the razor frequently to avoid clogs and reapply shaving cream as needed.

10. Once you’re done, hop back in the shower to rinse everything away.

11. Apply a moisturizer or body oil to the area to help keep it protected. You may also want to apply a moisturizer or anti-chafe product regularly (like at least once a day) to help reduce friction, which can cause irritation on shaved skin, especially below the belt.

Maybe you’re a regular manscaper, or perhaps you just took the plunge into trimming out your nether regions. Regardless, one truth holds true: As soon as you take off the hair, it blooms right back again.

Sure, it might seem that your pubic hair is on a steroid-fueled regrowth. But that’s actually something of an optic illusion, says Dr. Alexes Hazen, MD, a reconstructive and cosmetic plastic surgeon at NYU Langone Health.

People who trim or shave their pubic hair often believe it grows faster than the hair on their head, but that’s a misconception, she says. We merely notice hair growth more and its speed when it’s shorter.

With pubic hair—and other body hair—the entire process takes about 30 to 44 days, Dr. Hazen says. That means the same pubes that started to grow will shed in about a month to a month and a half.

#5117. Three Central Banks Test a Bridge Between Traditional FX and Tokenized Settlement

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The Bank of England, Monetary Authority of Singapore and Bank of Thailand have completed a cross-border foreign-exchange settlement experiment designed to connect existing payment infrastructure with tokenised systems. The project might sound technical, but it addresses a familiar financial problem: two parties need to exchange different currencies without either being exposed to the risk that one side pays and the other does not.

The trial offers evidence that traditional central-bank settlement systems and distributed ledgers can be coordinated in a controlled setting. It does not mean a new public FX network has launched or that ordinary customers can use the prototype today.

In their joint announcement, the three central banks described work under the Meridian FX APAC initiative. The experiment tested how payment-versus-payment settlement could function across different systems, including a distributed-ledger environment and conventional real-time gross settlement arrangements. Payment-versus-payment means one currency leg is settled only if the other can be settled too.

That principle is not new. What is new here is the attempt to apply it when separate technology stacks are involved. As the industry experiments with tokenised deposits and other digital representations of money, mismatches between systems can create delays or counterparty risks. A synchronised approach seeks to reduce that gap without requiring every participant to migrate onto the same ledger.

The trial also explored multilateral netting. Rather than having every participant settle each obligation individually, a system can calculate offsetting positions so that fewer funds need to move. In principle, this reduces liquidity demands and can make cross-border payment arrangements more efficient. In practice, netting depends on legal finality, settlement windows and clear responsibilities if a participant fails.

Partior developed the prototype used in the trial, according to reporting on the project. This was a test environment, not a new production service from the central banks. Each jurisdiction's live payment systems and regulatory frameworks would still need to support any eventual deployment, which makes the operational path more complicated than a successful demonstration might suggest.

Much of the industry's attention has been directed at tokenising bonds, shares or funds. Yet creating a digital security does not solve the equally important problem of settling the cash side of a transaction. If a tokenised asset settles instantly but payment remains trapped in an overnight banking process, a large part of the efficiency claim disappears.

That is why central-bank experiments deserve attention even from readers who do not trade foreign exchange. European work on tokenisation standards covered by NewsBTC reflects a related concern: interoperable rules and infrastructure are needed if digital securities are to operate beyond isolated pilots.

The Bank of England has discussed a synchronisation interface with a target timeline in 2028. That is a useful reminder of the gap between a promising proof of concept and regulated, always-available payment infrastructure. Security controls, access criteria and recovery procedures are as important as transaction speed.

For businesses, the near-term value is the direction of travel rather than an immediately available product. Stablecoin payment networks are already being used in commercial contexts, but central-bank settlement operates with distinct legal and systemic requirements. Meridian FX APAC shows institutions are working on the bridge between those worlds — carefully, and not yet at full scale.

#5116. XRP Exchange Balances Hit Yearly High, but Long-Term Holders Stay Put

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Exchange Balances Hit Yearly High, but Long-Term Holders Stay Put

XRP exchange balances have reached a one-year high, while the share of tokens untouched for over a year nears its annual peak.

XRP held on exchanges has reached a one-year high even as the share of coins untouched for more than a year approaches its own annual peak, according to figures cited by wealth-focused commentator Kamilah Stevenson.

Her latest video examines that split following a roughly 10% price decline, arguing that investors’ financial circumstances can matter as much as their market convictions.

Stevenson cites CryptoQuant data showing approximately 11.8 billion XRP on exchanges, the highest balance in a year. That puts more tokens within easy reach of trading, although exchange deposits alone do not establish that holders intend to sell.

Meanwhile, Glassnode figures cited in the video put the share of XRP unmoved for more than a year at roughly 56%, up from 51% in January. Stevenson also says XRP exchange-traded funds still hold about 1.19 billion tokens, despite a small outflow ending a reported 13-week inflow streak.

“Both groups saw the same price,” she says. “They reacted to it in completely opposite ways.”

The contrast is striking, but the metrics have limits. Coins remaining stationary demonstrate inactivity, not necessarily fresh buying or confidence, and neither measure establishes where XRP’s price goes next.

Dr. Stevenson identifies three recurring sources of selling pressure: leverage, investing money needed for near-term expenses, and entering a volatile market without a plan.

She cites roughly $25.7 million in XRP liquidations on Binance during a recent sell-off as an example of positions being closed regardless of investors’ intentions.

Her broader bullish case rests partly on institutional activity involving Ripple and its RLUSD stablecoin.

The YouTube video names Standard Chartered, Cross River Bank and DriveWealth among firms involved in custody, banking or settlement developments.

Those developments should not be treated as equivalent to demand for XRP itself. Nor does institutional infrastructure guarantee that token prices will recover.

The most durable point is about liquidity: cash reserves and manageable exposure reduce the likelihood that an unexpected bill or margin call dictates a sale.

Exchange balances may signal potential selling pressure across the market; they cannot reveal which holders can afford to wait.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) has printed a death cross for the first time in 14 months on its daily chart. The 50 MA is below the 200 MA. This death cross follows the last signal, which was back in September 2025.

The latest death cross signal coincides with a sharp price drop, with Shiba Inu falling to unusually low levels below $0.000004.

Cryptocurrencies tumbled over the weekend, with Shiba Inu dropping sharply to a low of $0.0000037 on Saturday, marking four straight days of declines since November 11.

A death cross was completed on its daily chart, reflecting the ongoing selling pressure in the market. Crypto has been pummeled in recent weeks by a confluence of factors; liquidations accelerated over the last 24 hours, reaching a total of $1.96 billion across the market, according to CoinGlass data.

Unlike the abrupt crashes that have punctuated previous crypto downturns, much of the preceding decline unfolded during relatively subdued trading before liquidations accelerated in recent days.

It remains to be seen whether buying power returns to the market. According to Bitwise CEO Matt Hougan, "There will be a big buying opportunity at some point, but it's hard to say when."

Shiba Inu rebounded from a low of $0.0000037 on Sunday, but the meme coin remains down 6.87% over the last 24 hours and down 14% over the week.

Further recovery will occur if dip buying gains traction, with the daily 50 MA and 200 MA at $0.000005 marking resistance levels for SHIB's price. Support is expected at $0.000003 if the declines continue.

Bitcoin [BTC] closed in the red for the third consecutive day, with its price sliding to $67,000 on the charts. So far, the fall in prices has been driven by both whales and retail traders.

However, this pattern could be changing soon as Bitcoin’s sentiment starts to flip gradually. For instance, Hyperliquid whales turned back to the net long after two weeks of shorting BTC. This was the first selling period for them since March.

In fact, the daily mean of net long and net short grew from -1700 BTC on 8th November to around 900 BTC at press time. This seemed to imply that whales have been buying the dip below $70,000.

During the rally, which started in August, these whales went long. They subsequently sold the top. However, that does not guarantee that they will be right again.

On the other hand, retail traders have been showing signs of capitulation. In fact, BTC’s monthly change in Retail Investor Demand declined to around -10% after a sharp rise to over 17% as the price approached $80,000.

The same is the weakest reading since March. Back then too, Hyperliquid whales were net short on BTC.

This fall in participation by retailers, volumes below $10K, have been common during BTC’s correction.

When looking at historical patterns, it is clearly evident that when retailers capitulate, the prices tend to reverse. Thus, going against the crowd may help investors catch a move, either to the downside or the upside early enough.

Still, that does not mean that the contrarian signal always works. Even though it may be an ideal time to build positions.

Moreover, Bitcoin‘s Open Interest (OI) on Binance fell to $8.30 billion from $9.60 billion in November alone. This was its lowest level since 18th August, when BTC exploded past $65,000.

The slide below $68,000 triggered more long liquidations after those on the previous day. Over the past 24 hours, $1 billion were wiped out in crypto, with longs accounting for $863.3 million against $144.2 million in shorts.

This action forced leveraged traders out as supported by the sharp decline in OI. So, if BTC price stabilizes while OI stays at these levels, it would mean a rebound will be driven more by spot demand than leverage.

Therefore, whale positioning and retail capitulation could be a signal for a sustainable BTC recovery.

However, it needs to be backed by capital inflows from the market in the form of ETFs and spot buying, among others.

#5113. Could Bitcoin Mining Use Scotland’s Stranded Wind Power? The Debate Is Heating Up

Scotland produces substantial amounts of wind power, yet parts of that generation are sometimes curtailed because the electricity grid cannot move it to the places where demand exists. A new policy argument suggests Bitcoin miners could provide a flexible buyer for power that might otherwise go unused. The proposal is attracting attention because curtailment is expensive, but the economics are more complicated than simply turning spare electricity into digital coins.

The idea comes from industry advocates, not from an announced government programme. Whether it would reduce costs for consumers depends on location, grid rules, emissions and what miners would actually pay for the electricity.

When transmission capacity is constrained, grid operators may pay generators to reduce output even when the wind is blowing. The system still has to maintain balance and ensure that power can reach customers safely. CoinDesk reported on an argument from the Bitcoin Policy Institute that flexible mining could help consume some of the energy affected by Scotland's network bottlenecks.

The reported cost of curtailment can exceed £1 billion a year, but that should not be mistaken for a pot of money miners could simply recover. Some payments arise from complex system constraints, and installing a new industrial load will not necessarily remove the need for other balancing actions. A credible proposal requires location-specific modelling rather than a national headline number.

Bitcoin mining machines can, in principle, reduce consumption quickly when electricity becomes scarce or valuable elsewhere. They do not depend on uninterrupted processing in quite the same way as many conventional businesses. That gives miners a potential role as interruptible customers, willing to operate when power is cheap and switch off at times of peak demand.

But the equipment needs reliable commercial arrangements to justify its capital cost. A facility operating only during unpredictable periods of curtailment may earn too little to cover machines, buildings, cooling and maintenance. The central question is how many hours of usable electricity would be available and at what total delivered cost after grid charges and other expenses.

Using energy that would otherwise be curtailed could be beneficial under certain conditions, yet it does not automatically make a mining site carbon-neutral. The actual comparison depends on the electricity mix, whether the new demand changes generator behaviour, the facility's operating schedule and the alternatives for the power. Grid reinforcement, batteries and other demand-response projects may compete to solve the same problem.

The broader mining sector is already weighing energy against new computing opportunities. NewsBTC recently covered MARA's Bitcoin sales and AI data-centre plans, while another report examined an AI-focused shift at Hyperscale Data. These moves show that miners are increasingly being judged as power and infrastructure operators as well as Bitcoin producers.

Before declaring success, any Scottish mining proposal would need transparent figures for curtailment hours, transmission capacity, tariffs, environmental impacts and the ability to curtail the mine itself. It would also need to explain who captures the benefit: the miner, the generator, the network operator or bill payers. Those answers could support a limited trial, or show that another use of the electricity is better.

The debate is worthwhile because renewable generation and grid capacity are growing at different speeds. Bitcoin mining could be one tool in a larger flexibility toolkit. Presenting it as a guaranteed cure for Scotland's grid costs would be several steps ahead of the evidence.

#5112. The 12 Best Underwear for Men, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Boxer briefs from Mack Weldon and Calvin Klein came out on top in our testing.

I’VE WORN ENOUGH bad underwear to know it can sabotage your entire day. This is the layer that determines whether you’re comfortable or constantly readjusting before anything else goes on. And yet, most men stick with the same underwear type from college. Meanwhile, the category has evolved. Today’s best underwear is softer, stretchier, and far more breathable, with odor-fighting tech and support that cradles your crown jewels without the squeeze. If you haven’t upgraded lately, your top drawer is probably long overdue for a refresh.

At Men’s Health, we’ve been testing underwear since 2015, and I’ve personally cycled through more pairs than I can count—part of a larger pool spanning 50-plus brands and 100-plus styles, from newer names like Skims to longtime staples like Calvin Klein. Year after year, our biggest takeaway stays the same: the pairs worth buying stay put, feel smooth from morning to night, and remain in great shape after a few spins through the wash. Whether you’re a boxer-briefs guy, a loose-boxers loyalist, or somewhere in between, this is one piece you don’t want to get wrong.

Out of the hundreds of skivvies we've tested since 2018, the Airknitx Boxer Brief came out on top for its comfort, support, and breathability. I’ve worn it to work, during workout classes, and everywhere in between. One feature I appreciate is the supportive pouch, which comfortably cradles the family jewels without suffocating them. It skips the front fly that gives you quicker, easier access when using the bathroom, but the tradeoff is a cleaner, sharper fit. The polyamide-elastane fabric has a mesh-like texture that keeps you cool and dry, instead of soaking up sweat during intense movement. Even during a four-mile run on the treadmill, this pair never once felt overheated, swampy, or in a rush to change. The waist feels secure without rolling, while the grippy leg bands keep everything in place without squeezing your thighs.

Like the name suggests, the brief feels light as air. It’s insanely soft on the skin, and the cut is also flattering on the thighs for guys with beefy quads. To really seal the deal, Mack Weldon even incorporated mesh cool zones in the back to boost airflow and help prevent odors when temperatures climb. Overall, it’s a functional pair built for everything under the sun: daily wear, hot weather, sleeping, gym workouts, long-haul flights, outdoor adventures, and the list continues. Plus, there's a vast color selection of solids and heathers, which go with just about any casual and business casual fit.

Sometimes, sticking with an OG brand is the smartest move. And when it comes to underwear, it's impossible to fail with a pair from Calvin Klein. As the pioneer of sexy basics that won us over with celebrity campaigns, we love its stretch boxer brief for its seriously smooth cotton-spandex fabric.

Our testers say this boxer brief is super comfortable and breathable. The stretch is another big win. The 4D Flex Microfiber mesh boxer briefs from Polo Ralph Lauren will keep you cool from sunup to sundown. What really sets it apart is the stretch. It's tuned just right: never saggy, never constrictive, and it stays put whether I'm hitting the gym, playing tennis, or running errands. Tommy John earned the crown for the best overall pajamas due to their übersoft second-skin fabric, so it's no shock that the brand's underwear exceeds our expectations, too. Unlike other trunks that call for constant tugging or readjusting, these stayed perfectly in place, whether we were sitting, standing, or running errands around town. Despite us breaking a sweat, this underwear stayed fresh, which speaks to their exceptional level of odor resistance. And even after multiple washes, the softness doesn't diminish—a true sign of premium quality.

Sunspel’s Classic Boxer Shorts are hands down some of the best out there, and once you try them, you’ll get it. This pair is made by a U.K. brand with over a century of experience perfecting the essentials, so it's time-tested. These boxers are cut from long-staple cotton, meaning the fibers are longer, the fabric is softer, and it'll last for the long haul. Basically, it feels ridiculously comfortable—like you’re lounging in luxury every time you put it on—and it stays that way wear after wear.

One standout feature is the distinctive back panel. Sunspel uses a single smooth panel across the rear versus an uncomfortable central seam running down the middle. For us, that meant no chafing, no awkward pressure, and no irritation, even when we were sitting at our work desk or running quick errands. The fabric is lightweight but strong, so it breathes well and never bunches under pants. During testing, it held up all day, no matter what: long commutes, walking tours on vacation, or casual bike rides. We don't recommend wearing this pair under gym shorts, but you can reserve it for days of less sweat-inducing activity since it's all cotton.

They’ve got this easy, relaxed fit that gives you full range of motion, but the tailoring keeps them from feeling baggy or sloppy. And then there’s the design: They’re finished with a super gentle waistband that sits comfortably. We also love that there's solid colors as well as striped patterns. It's the kind that makes you rethink the whole category. They’re built for comfort but stylish enough to feel special, which is exactly what you want from a pair you’ll wear day in and day out.

I normally wouldn’t trust underwear that costs under $10 to compete with premium pairs, but Uniqlo’s trunks are the exception. The Japanese retailer offers some of the best basics around, delivering impressive quality at an affordable price, including these boxer shorts, which are especially comfortable in the heat. They’re made with a breathable woven cotton fabric, which feels much lighter than any knit underwear I own. When the temps went up to 100 degrees in New York last week, these kept me cool all day.

The fit is more open and roomy than my briefs, so my crown jewels had plenty of breathing room and even caught a breeze when I was lounging around. I also love how they lie flat under shorts and linen pants, though I would skip wearing slim trousers since the fabric can bunch. Even though the waistband is scrunched, it sits gently against my skin without causing any irritation. When my Sunspel pair is in the laundry, I’ll even wear it to bed on warm nights. For such an inexpensive style, it holds up over time. I’ve washed it multiple times without seeing a single loose seam or noticing any shrinkage. Plus, the striped pattern looks timeless, so it doesn’t feel like a bargain-bin underwear.

I can always count on mesh fabric to keep me cool when I need it most, which is why I love this underwear. SAXX uses a polyester-elastane mesh with an open, dotted texture that lets heat and moisture escape, so I never feel clammy. Even when I sweat, the fabric never gets waterlogged and dries incredibly fast. It’s one of my go-to pairs for workouts, especially on heavy cardio days. The hammock-style pouch keeps everything secure and supported while I’m biking or running on the treadmill, and the fit is snugger than most boxer shorts, specifically around the butt, thigh, and legs.

The 6-inch inseam stops mid-thigh, while the high waist sits right under your belly button. I can wear them under just about any pair of pants without worrying about bunching or visible lines. The compression-like fit may feel too snug if you prefer a roomier boxer short. And the mesh fabric isn’t as soft or natural-feeling as cotton or modal, so it may not be everyone’s favorite pair for lounging all day. The good thing is the pack of three can get you through half the week, especially if you stock up.

If you’re ready to upgrade from basic cotton underwear, CDLP is where I’d start. I love the Tencel Lyocell fabric that has an incredibly silky, almost cooling feel against my skin. It’s surprisingly breathable, too, so I never feel overheated on days when the temps spike to 90 degrees. It strikes a nice balance between feeling luxurious and being practical. The snug fit hugs my body without squeezing too tightly. It rests just below the waist and has a 3.8-inch inseam that sits high on the upper thigh and hides under my short shorts. Some of the more expensive pairs tend to pill, but the fabric on this one keeps its smooth, premium feel even after multiple washes. The only real drawback is the price, but if you’re willing to splurge on a single pair of underwear, the comfort makes it feel well worth it.

Quality underwear doesn't have to cost a fortune. Take Uniqlo's Airism Ultra Seamless Boxer Briefs, which clock in under $20 and also fit like a glove. During my testing, the cutoff waist felt invisible, sitting flush against the skin without squeezing or rolling, like it was made just for me. Despite its close-hugging cut, there's a fair amount of stretch to accommodate you running up the stairs, twisting in your chair, or walking briskly through crowded city streets.

Overall, I found this pair to be lightweight, super breathable, and packed with new moisture-wicking technology that helps to keep you fresh, cool, and dry around the clock. Whether it's a hot day or you're working up a sweat at the gym, Airism pulls moisture away from your skin, making sure you don't feel swampy down under.

Every Sunday at my house is wash day, but this underwear has survived through every last cycle without losing its allure. Our only gripe is that Uniqlo Airism sells out very fast, which means you have to wait for the occasional restock—so get them now.

Cotton is the OG of underwear fabrics, and our testers found that it's the most comfortable knit for everyday fits. Take note: while cotton is pretty breathable, it doesn't do a great job of wicking away moisture. That's why our fashion editors do not recommend cotton skivvies for working out. In some cases, a pair of undies that's 100% cotton tends to lose shape over time and can give a swamp-ass feeling. If you have money to spend, we recommend trying a long-staple or organic cotton, which is more premium and durable.

Nylon is moisture-wicking and super durable, so the fabric won’t pill or stretch out. However, a little spandex (aka elastane) in the fabric helps for movement and extra comfort. Plus, it dries quickly too, so you won't feel sticky post-workout.

Imagine cotton, but smoother and a little fancier. Modal has a silky-soft feel that's light and cool against your skin. Testers say their favorite modal boxer briefs almost disappear under their clothes.

If you're looking to keep your precious cargo secure, then briefs provide the most security. However, if you want to let the package breathe, then boxers are your best bet. Remember: Boxers tend to ride up when you're wearing slim pants, which is why we recommend only wearing them with more relaxed fits.

If you need extra support, we recommend underwear with a pouch or a snugger fit around the waistband. For some men with testicular pain or discomfort, they may want to find a style that fits well and doesn't ride up or bunch, as this could aggravate their symptoms.

Your underwear is the first thing you put on and the last thing you take off, so it has to work with you, not against you, all day long. If it doesn't do its job, you'll feel it, whether it's discomfort, chafing, or overheating.

Think about it: excellent underwear isn't just about looking cool (though that's like icing on the cake). It's about how it performs in real life. Are you lounging at home? Going for a long run? Stuck on a flight for hours? Each of these scenarios demands something different. You need underwear that supports your lifestyle, whether that's stretch for flexibility, moisture-wicking for sweat, or breathability to keep things fresh down yonder.

The best breathable underwear manages heat and moisture so sweat can escape instead of getting trapped against your skin. Many use micro-knit or mesh-like weaves that create tiny air channels within the fabric, allowing heat to dissipate and air to circulate as you move. Others incorporate moisture-wicking fibers to pull sweat away from the body and spread it across the surface of the fabric so it evaporates faster. Some brands even add targeted “cool zones” or thinner panels in high-sweat areas to boost airflow where you need it most.

When underwear can’t breathe, moisture builds up, leading to overheating, chafing, irritation, and odor. Breathable underwear works with your body by keeping things cooler, drier, and more comfortable throughout the day. For Men’s Health guys, breathability makes a difference for everyday wear, long commutes, desk jobs, workouts, travel days, and humid conditions. It’s especially clutch for guys who sweat easily, live in hot climates, train hard, or spend long stretches in the same pair from morning to night.

As part of the Men’s Health style team, led by our Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, I’ve tested some of the best—and worst—underwear on the market firsthand. Since 2015, our team has worn, washed, and stressed-tested more than 100 pairs across every major style, brand, and fabric imaginable, from classic cotton briefs to high-tech performance boxer briefs and luxe everyday upgrades.

Testing wasn't limited to just one body type or fit preference. In addition to my own wear tests, multiple Men's Health editors with different builds pitched in, spanning sizes from small through XXL. This allowed us to see how each pair fit and performed across a wide range of body types, rises, thigh sizes, and proportions—and to flag issues like inconsistent sizing, rolling waistbands, or fabric that only works on one kind of frame.

I wore each pair repeatedly in real-life situations, including workdays, workouts, commutes, travel, and weekend outings. I looked at how each pair performed over time, paying close attention to whether fabrics remained soft without pilling, waistbands held their shape, seams avoided chafing, and support held up after hours of movement. I judged each pair on fabric quality, fit, breathability, odor control, stretch and recovery, durability after repeated washes, and comfort levels ranging from morning to night. Only the pairs that consistently delivered comfort, support, and long-term performance earned a spot on this list. What you’ll find here are the top 12 best men’s underwear options that rose to the top after years of hands-on testing by the Men’s Health team.

Boxers: They’re classic, loose-fitting shorts that are lightweight, with lots of breathing room, and zero restriction. They’re great for lounging or sleeping because they feel airy and relaxed, but that same looseness makes them less practical under slim pants. Fabric can bunch, ride up, and offer little to no support if you’re moving around a lot. Boxer briefs: They’re cut like boxers but fit snugly like briefs. That means they hug your thighs, hold everything in place, and layer smoothly under jeans, trousers, or even gym shorts. They also prevent chafing since the fabric creates a barrier between your thighs—a lifesaver if you walk a lot or hit the gym. The tradeoff? They’re less airy than boxers, but most guys prefer the balance of comfort, coverage, and support.

That really depends on your laundry schedule. If you’re someone who does laundry once a week, aim for at least 10 to 12 pairs so you’ve got a little cushion. If laundry happens less often—say every two weeks—you’ll probably want 15 to 20 pairs. If you’re very active, then consider stocking your drawer with 25 to 30 pairs. Basically, you want enough to last until wash day plus a couple extra for workouts, surprise trips, or the occasional lazy Sunday when you just don’t feel like doing laundry.

A good rule of thumb: it’s reasonable to refresh your stash every six to 12 months, but quality underwear can last longer depending on fabric, frequency of wear, washing, and condition. If the elastic’s shot, they’re sagging, developing holes, or the fabric’s thinning, that’s your cue to toss them. Think of it as a rotation—you don’t need to replace everything at once, but gradually swap in new pairs so you’re always stocked with comfortable, supportive ones.

Every man has worn them at some point; boxers are light and loose and so freeing. They're the classic underwear style for men that feels very relaxed with short legs. This type of underwear is perfect for lounging around the house, sleeping, or wearing under relaxed-fit pants. Also comes in a variety of prints and patterns (hello, personality).

Think speedo. Think upside-down triangle. Briefs provide the required coverage and optimal support while exposing more skin for ease of mobility. Here, there's no risk of leg fabric riding up (because there's none).

Perhaps the most popular one, it's a hybrid of loose-fit boxers and tight briefs, offering a solid balance of support and comfort. If you’re not a fan of underwear that rides up too high, go for boxer briefs that have a longer leg and a snug fit, like compression underwear that’s perfect for the gym. They should skim the leg versus squeezing you too tight.

Like the title says, a trunk is similar to boxer briefs but with a shorter cut—halfway up the thigh. It's best for guys who want something fitted but less fabric around the leg. For some visual assistance, think of trunks as the underwear style that most CK models wear on big billboards.

It depends on personal preference, comfort, and the activity. Here's a quick breakdown to help guide your choice, weighing the pros and cons of both.

Tight underwear (e.g., briefs, boxer briefs) provides better support, which is especially useful for physical activities like running or working out. This type reduces chafing and prevents excessive movement, which can help with comfort throughout the day. Works well under slim-fit pants, as it avoids bunching and creates a cleaner silhouette. If it's too tight, it can restrict airflow and potentially cause discomfort or sweating, especially in warmer weather. Overly tight fits might not be ideal for guys concerned about reproductive health, though the effect is typically negligible with properly sized underwear.

On the other hand, loose underwear is better suited for lounging or casual, low-impact activities since it allows more airflow and freedom of movement. It feels more breathable, making it ideal for hotter climates or relaxed settings. Also, loose underwear can be paired with loose-fit pants for added comfort. This option lacks support, which feel uncomfortable during workouts or physical activity. Plus, it can cramp your style—bunching up under tighter pants and offering a restrictive feel.

If you want to protect the structural integrity of your underwear's waistband, the best way to keep them from stretching is to hand wash them and hang them dry. But given how impractical that is, the second best option is to put them in the washing machine on cold water and use a low dryer setting so the elastic doesn't warp. However, our testers say that most of the pairs they've tried have kept their waistbands' shapes even after several trips to the laundromat. If your underwear's waistband has lost its shape, you're probably overdue to replace it.

Even the best underwear won’t last if you don’t take care of it properly. Washing underwear inside out helps remove sweat and bacteria more effectively while protecting the fabric’s surface. Cold or warm water is usually best, as hot water can break down elastic fibers and cause shrinkage over time. Skip harsh detergents and fabric softeners, especially for performance or moisture-wicking underwear. Softeners can coat fibers and reduce breathability and odor control. When possible, air-drying is ideal, as high heat from dryers is the fastest way to kill stretch and warp waistbands. If you do use a dryer, stick to low heat.

#5111. Cardano's Hoskinson Says Everyone Will Be Happy Next Year

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson is sending out a hopeful message to the crypto space in the wake of a brutal market crash that is causing ADA to come very close to falling out of the top 20 crypto assets.

Recently, Hoskinson took to X to respond to a frustrated Cardano fan who posted a screenshot showing ADA falling almost 10% in the last 24 hours.

“It’s all going to be ok,” said Hoskinson. “Everyone will be happy next year after all this madness, hate and idiocy.”

The recent crypto market crash has proven to be extremely brutal for a lot of different assets, and Cardano is certainly one of the worst affected.

In recent trading, ADA has fallen all the way down to around $0.15.

At these levels, ADA is currently down around 95% from its all-time high of $3.09, which was reached in September 2021, based on data from CoinGecko.

This represents an almost complete loss of investment value for those who bought at the all-time high.

Overall, Cardano is also down around 35% in the last month and almost 60% since the start of 2026.

As a result, Cardano’s market cap has fallen all the way down to around $5.7 billion, with ADA dropping to 18th place in CoinGecko’s crypto rankings.

This is a very precarious position for the once-dominant altcoin Cardano, which is now extremely close to falling out of the top 20.

It seems as though there are a few different factors at play behind Cardano’s poor performance.

First of all, there has been a huge sell-off in the broader crypto market. Bitcoin has seen major drops, leading to more selling pressure on major altcoins.

This decline has coincided with a falling technology stock market, ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty, outflows from crypto investment products, and mass liquidations of leveraged positions.

That said, there are clearly some issues with Cardano beyond the wider market struggles.

For one, Cardano has faced a lot of criticism over the years for the blockchain’s relatively low adoption, even after years of development. This is especially evident when compared to other chains like Ethereum and Solana.

In fact, Cardano’s decentralized finance ecosystem has recently seen around $46 million in total value locked, as reported by DefiLlama.

Elsewhere, Hoskinson recently found himself embroiled in another controversy surrounding Cardano’s future.

In another recent X post, Hoskinson lashed out at certain commentators who keep bashing the blockchain for its apparent lack of adoption.

He noted that critics initially claimed Cardano suffered from poor on-chain metrics, few real-world use cases and technology that no one wanted to use.

Then, when Hoskinson decided to work on developing apps that would be able to attract millions of people and billions in assets, it seemed as though those same critics began claiming he was scamming everyone.

“You people are both stupid and scum. I can’t fix stupid,” said Hoskinson. “Grow up.”

Ripple’s Ripple Prime institutional crypto brokerage platform is witnessing a major change. Ripple Prime founder Marc Asch is going to leave the position at year-end as Noel Kimmel assumes leadership.

Noel Kimmel, already serving as Vice President of Ripple Prime, will assume leadership of the business and their team within Ripple Labs. This marks Ripple Prime’s transition from a regular custody & brokerage platform to major-scale financial services & infrastructure provider.

Marc Asch founded Hidden Road back in 2018, instantly becoming the growing brokerage’s CEO. The company offered a wide variety of digital-asset powered services, including foreign exchange, derivatives and fixed income. Ripple made a deal to acquire the platform in 2025.

Since the massive acquisition, Ripple Labs expanded the newly-acquired subsidiary’s business towards leveraged ETF financing. The branch even processed $13 trillion in payments during 2025, but the vague regulations kept all of that trading action outside of crypto’s boundaries.

Ripple Prime founder Marc Asch is stepping down at year end, per CoinDesk, with Noel Kimmel taking over the prime brokerage Ripple bought for $1.25B in 2025. Founders leaving a year after a sale is normal. The test is whether institutions keep growing there. Red flag or nothing?

Right now, Ripple Prime serves over 300 institutions worldwide. The freshly-appointed CEO Noel Kimmel was already deeply involved in this expansion. He previously represented Ripple Prime in its $200 million financing agreement, designed to raise institutional margin capacity.

The brokerage platform went on to introduce equity-linked derivatives and financing for Ripple’s institutional customers. Another key milestone was the deal with Brevan Howard, an accounting company looking after $35 billion in assets under management (AUM) for clearing services.

#5108. JPMorgan Filing Shows Bigger Strategy Stake and $540 Million in Bitcoin ETF Shares

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

A quarterly US securities filing has put fresh numbers around JPMorgan's exposure to crypto-linked investments. The filing shows larger reported positions in both Strategy, the Bitcoin treasury company, and BlackRock's spot Bitcoin ETF at the end of September. The figures are significant, but they need to be read with care: a Form 13F records reportable investment holdings at a particular date, not a continuous record of what a bank or its customers are buying today.

That nuance is especially important when headlines about large financial institutions are used as shorthand for bullish conviction. The disclosure tells us what was reported, but not necessarily who made each underlying investment decision or why.

The Block reported that JPMorgan's September 30 filing listed 848,932 Strategy shares, up from 624,387 in the previous quarter. The reported value was about $131.3 million. It also listed roughly 11.4 million shares of BlackRock's IBIT spot Bitcoin trust, with a quarter-end value around $540 million and a share-count increase of approximately 9.6%.

Those figures should not be mistaken for half a billion dollars of direct Bitcoin held in a wallet controlled by the bank. IBIT shares are securities that provide exposure through a fund structure. Strategy shares are equity in a company with a substantial Bitcoin treasury and its own operating and financing risks. Both can be influenced by Bitcoin, but neither is identical to owning a BTC coin on-chain.

Institutional investment managers disclose certain US-listed positions on Form 13F after a quarter ends. That means the most recent figures in this story reflect September 30 holdings, not positions on November 15. The filing does not show every asset or liability a reporting entity might have, and it cannot tell readers whether any listed shares were subsequently sold.

It also does not automatically establish that JPMorgan's own proprietary balance sheet made a particular directional bet. Reportable holdings may relate to investment management and other activities. Distinguishing those arrangements is essential before drawing conclusions about corporate strategy or client preferences.

Strategy provides a corporate route to Bitcoin exposure, but its share price also responds to debt issuance, financing terms, dilution and market expectations about its treasury model. NewsBTC's coverage of benchmark decisions involving Strategy and Metaplanet highlights a further variable: index rules can affect demand for company shares independently of the Bitcoin price itself.

An ETF operates differently. Fund shares seek to track the underlying Bitcoin exposure subject to fees and market mechanics, without conferring ownership of the issuer's broader business. An institution holding both securities might be accessing two different kinds of risk, or serving clients with different mandates. The filing alone does not reveal that motivation.

Bitcoin's price and the appetite for crypto products have deteriorated markedly since September. NewsBTC's reporting on November's spot ETF redemptions is a reminder that institutional positioning can change quickly. A larger September holding can coexist with substantial industry-wide outflows in November without either dataset being incorrect.

The sensible next step is to compare successive filings and separate share-count changes from valuation changes. Readers should also watch how managers describe their exposures, rather than attributing motives from the raw totals. This 13F offers useful evidence of institutional participation in crypto-linked securities. It is not a real-time endorsement of the current Bitcoin price.

#5104. Senate Hearing Could Shape the SEC’s Next Chapter for Crypto Oversight

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The US Senate Banking Committee is preparing to examine nominees for positions at the Securities and Exchange Commission, a development that could eventually influence the tone and priorities of crypto oversight. A hearing scheduled for Thursday, November 19, puts personnel decisions back in the spotlight at a time when industry participants are seeking clearer rules on token offerings, custody and trading venues.

Hearings are part of the appointment process, not the end of it. An appearance before senators does not amount to confirmation, and nominees' eventual influence will depend on their responsibilities, the agency's composition and the laws it must enforce.

CoinDesk reported that the Banking Committee had scheduled a November 19 hearing involving SEC nominees Steven Levine and Kristin Johnson. The proceedings are expected to give senators an opportunity to question the candidates on their approach to securities regulation, though what they actually say should be judged from the hearing record rather than predicted in advance.

The same reporting discussed separate nominees for roles at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The CFTC's appointment process is not identical to the SEC's, and a hearing for one agency should not be read as an automatic timetable for the other. Both agencies affect digital-asset activity, but their legal jurisdictions and responsibilities differ.

Businesses building token markets often want to know which rules apply before launching a product, not after it has attracted users. Questions can include whether an asset or particular transaction falls within securities law, how intermediaries should register and what disclosures are expected. Regulatory staff and commissioners shape policy through rulemaking, enforcement decisions and public guidance, although courts and Congress also have important roles.

A change in personnel can influence priorities, but it does not instantly rewrite the rules. Existing statutes remain in force, earlier litigation can continue and new policy proposals may need formal procedures. For a company considering a US product launch, a nomination is therefore a signal to monitor rather than a substitute for legal advice or an enacted regulation.

Prediction markets and derivative instruments illustrate the difficulty of drawing clear regulatory lines. NewsBTC's earlier coverage of litigation involving Coinbase, Kalshi and the CFTC demonstrates how novel products can trigger disputes over oversight and market structure. The SEC and CFTC do not necessarily reach the same questions through the same legal framework.

International developments also provide a reminder that the United States does not set standards in isolation. European tokenisation discussions covered by NewsBTC show regulators elsewhere trying to align traditional financial protections with new technology. US appointees will face the task of balancing market integrity, investor protection and innovation against a global competitive backdrop.

Specific answers about custody, market intermediaries, token distributions and enforcement philosophy would be more informative than general pledges to support innovation or protect consumers. Written responses and subsequent votes are worth watching too. Yet even a persuasive performance at a hearing offers no guarantee of confirmation or a particular policy outcome.

The near-term event is clear: November 19 provides a public checkpoint for the SEC nominees. What follows may shape the regulatory conversation over months and years. Treating a personnel hearing as an immediate market catalyst would be a much bigger claim than the available evidence supports.

#5102. 2026 was supposed to be the year of altcoins – So what went wrong?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

For years, investors in the crypto market have followed a familiar pattern. The moment they see that Bitcoin’s price gains are eventually slowing down, they begin moving capital into Ethereum and other altcoins in search of higher returns.

This rotation has historically fueled what the market calls an “altcoin season.”

However, 2026 is beginning to challenge that expectation. Though the market has seen brief periods of outperformance, these have failed to develop into a sustained rally across the wider altcoin ecosystem.

What makes this particularly concerning is that the year is now approaching its end without a convincing sign of the long-awaited rotation.

To understand the case better first, let’s focus on the total altcoin market capitalization, which fell from approximately $1.85 trillion to $1.06 trillion in just a month, erasing almost around $800 billion in value.

At the same time, the Altcoin Season Index has struggled to maintain readings above the 75 threshold, which traditionally signals an altcoin season.

At press time, too, the index was sitting at 48, which means that the Bitcoin [BTC] season continues to be in full swing at the moment despite BTC trading at $73,836.99 at press time.

This came after a recent report by AMBCrypto, which indicated that the median altcoin’s returns by November had dropped slightly below Bitcoin and that both Bitcoin’s 60-day returns and the altcoin’s returns had returned to zero.

Going back in time, the years 2021 and 2023 delivered substantial rallies during different parts of the year. However, the year 2022 remained dominated by bearish sentiment. Moving forward, the end of 2024 is what provides an important point of comparison.

Following Bitcoin’s move above $100,000 in December, market attention expanded towards Ethereum [ETH], XRP, Solana, and other large-cap altcoins. And the broader market entered 2025 with considerable optimism around a potential continuation of that rotation.

However, the experience of 2025 also demonstrated that such rallies are not necessarily sustained. Glassnode’s historical analysis highlighted that altcoin trading volume had previously surged to nearly four times Bitcoin’s volume around September 2025, before cooling as Bitcoin approached its October market top.

The same pattern appeared in September 2026. Altcoin spot volume again climbed to almost four times Bitcoin’s volume, suggesting a period of heightened speculation. By late October, however, the ratio had declined to approximately three times Bitcoin’s volume.

He warned that major altcoins are approaching critical support levels. For instance, Hyperliquid [HYPE] could fall to $64 or $53 if it breaks below $75, while Ondo [ONDO] risks dropping to $0.26 or $0.19 below $0.35. Quant [QNT] could also decline towards $160 if it breaks below $190.

These setups suggest that selling pressure is spreading beyond smaller tokens, making a broad-based altcoin recovery increasingly unlikely in 2026.

Echoing a similar sentiment, another crypto educator on X added,

Using CryptoQuant analysis, he suggested that altcoins have lost approximately $200 billion in market capitalization. Around 70% of Binance-listed altcoins are trading below their 200-day moving averages, while only 13.2% of the top 250 crypto assets recorded positive returns in October.

Then, one of the strongest arguments against an imminent altcoin season is Bitcoin’s continued dominance. At press time too, Bitcoin dominance was around 60.98%.

That said, execs in the crypto communities are also increasingly questioning whether the traditional altcoin cycle is still relevant.

For instance, Benjamin Cowen, founder & CEO of ITC, in his recent commentary, added to this concern, where he argued that the arrival of Q4 highlighted the weakness across the market, with altcoins facing greater pressure.

Unfortunately, with the cryptocurrency market witnessing approximately $738.92 million in liquidations over the past 24 hours, affecting 120,474 traders according to CoinGlass data, concerns are valid.

This is also because the largest altcoin, Ethereum, recorded the highest liquidations at $261.27 million, followed by Bitcoin at $204.45 million. Additionally, Solana [SOL] and Zcash also saw significant liquidations of $38.93 million and $39.47 million, respectively.

Then there is another caveat to figure out, and that is where investors are directing their money.

Well, in the month of November so far, BTC ETFs recorded the largest outflow worth approximately $1.58 billion, followed by ETH ETFs at $551.10 million. Among altcoins, HYPE ETFs saw $18.25 million in outflows, XRP ETFs recorded $18.57 million, while Hedera [HBAR] ETFs registered $2.83 million.

Chainlink [LINK], Avalanche [AVAX], Litecoin [LTC], and Binance [BNB] also recorded smaller outflows. This suggests that investors were withdrawing capital across both Bitcoin and altcoins rather than rotating into smaller cryptocurrencies.

At the same time, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index was standing at ‘Fear’ at 29 at press time. These indicators reinforce one another and suggest that the traditional altcoin season is losing its momentum.

#5100. Meta’s Internal Prediction App Uses Points, Not Cash — and That Distinction Matters

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Meta is reportedly experimenting with a prediction game for employees in which participants forecast outcomes using points rather than real money. That may sound like a small internal product test, but it offers an interesting window into how large technology companies are thinking about forecasting, social engagement and the mechanics behind prediction markets.

The essential distinction is that a points-based game is not automatically a cash-settled financial market. No public launch or real-money service has been confirmed in the reporting on the experiment, so it would be misleading to describe Meta as having entered the regulated betting or event-contract business.

The Block, citing The Wall Street Journal, reported that Meta was testing an employee application known as Takes, previously called Arena. Participants can make forecasts and earn or lose an internal points balance referred to as cred. The structure resembles a prediction market in some respects, but without the same money flows or legal arrangements as a traded contract.

An internal trial can help answer useful product questions. Do people enjoy making forecasts? How should results be scored? Does a ranking system reward genuine insight or simply encourage attention-grabbing guesses? Those questions matter whether the eventual outcome is a staff game, a public social feature or nothing at all. The existence of a test does not establish which direction Meta will choose.

Real-money prediction markets can involve financial risk, market manipulation concerns, customer eligibility, settlement disputes and questions about gambling or derivatives law. A points-based contest may avoid some of those features, depending on its design. But a game can still have integrity problems if employees feel encouraged to trade on private information or if forecasts become workplace performance signals.

There is also a difference between a prediction with a numerical score and a security or derivative. Those categories are shaped by contract terms and applicable law, not simply by whether the interface looks like a market. Readers should be cautious when comparing an internal staff experiment directly with companies offering event contracts to paying customers.

Regulated prediction markets are attracting scrutiny from federal and state authorities, particularly around sports-related contracts. NewsBTC previously examined a CFTC-related lawsuit involving Coinbase and Kalshi, an example of how disputes over jurisdiction can arise as firms offer products that do not fit neatly into traditional categories.

That uncertainty makes Meta's use of non-cash points noteworthy. A platform can learn about user participation and forecasting behaviour without immediately building the custody, settlement and compliance systems required for real-money products. Whether that is the strategic reason for the design has not been established; it is simply a material distinction between the two models.

Big companies routinely trial features that never reach the public. Employee feedback can reveal problems early, and an internal rename does not by itself mean a product is ready for commercial deployment. Similarly, parallels with AI-agent payment experiments covered by NewsBTC show how companies use small tests to explore unfamiliar transaction designs before the market is settled.

The next meaningful development would be an official description of the experiment's objectives, product scope or possible external release. Until then, Takes is best understood as a reported internal forecasting test — an interesting sign of curiosity, but not evidence that Meta has launched a new exchange.

According to CoinGlass, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on the Coinbase spot market reached -$1.08 billion between Oct. 31 and Nov. 15. CVD shows the difference between the volume of market buy orders and market sell orders, and a negative CVD means that sellers were more active on the exchange.

Over the same period, the CVD on the spot markets of OKX, Bybit and Binance stood at $240.3 million, $65.17 million and $51.88 million, respectively, so buyers were more active on these three exchanges.

The price of Bitcoin went down from $81,188 on Nov. 4 to $61,956 on Nov. 14, according to CoinGlass data, and the decline amounted to around 24%. On Sunday, Bitcoin recovered to around $65,400.

The data comes amid claims that Binance has been pushing the price of Bitcoin down. The exchange lost $6.4 billion in a hack on Oct. 29, and some users on X then claimed that Binance was selling crypto to cover its losses. Two weeks after the attack, Binance published a Proof of Reserves report that showed client balances on the exchange were fully backed.

This week, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao shared a comparison of Bitcoin charts ahead of the SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs and called it "an interesting analysis." Several users in the replies to his post blamed the drop in Bitcoin on selling by Binance.

Binance is the largest crypto exchange by trading volume, and a large share of futures liquidations takes place on the platform. On Nov. 13, crypto exchanges liquidated 187,389 traders for a total of $1.65 billion in 24 hours, and 88% of that amount came from long positions, according to CoinGlass. Still, the CVD on the Binance spot market has stayed positive since Oct. 31.

Coinbase is the custodian for most U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, including BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, and many U.S. institutional investors trade on the platform through Coinbase Prime.

Anthropic is set to start trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19, and the selling on Coinbase comes ahead of the listing. Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee has called the recent drawdown in Bitcoin a temporary rotation of money into mega-IPOs, and in the 50 days before the Anthropic IPO, Bitcoin has lost around 18%.

The CVD on Coinbase fell most sharply between Nov. 10 and Nov. 14, and Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 during this period, according to CoinGlass data.
